issue.title: In-process family hand-offs in the same wall-clock second share one artifacts directory, so the second successor overwrites the first's agent_meta.json
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-p8.6 (epic sase-p8, 'sase pipe'), routed here by that epic's land agent. NOT caused by that epic: the defect is in shared artifact-directory creation and predates pipe.

WHAT IS WRONG: create_artifacts_directory() in src/sase/artifacts.py:61 derives the directory name from datetime.now(get_timezone()).strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S') and then calls artifacts_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True). There is no collision suffix, no retry, and no uniqueness check. Two calls inside the same wall-clock second therefore resolve to the SAME path, and the second caller's write_agent_meta_atomic() in create_followup_artifacts (src/sase/axe/run_agent_helpers_artifacts.py:199) replaces the first successor's agent_meta.json rather than creating a sibling. The first successor's identity, role_suffix, relationships, and model metadata are lost.

WHO IS AFFECTED: every in-process family-successor hand-off shares this path, not just pipe — handle_accepted_plan's coder hand-off, handle_questions_marker's follow-up, the plan feedback replan branch in run_agent_exec_plan.py, and handle_pipe_marker all reach create_followup_artifacts. Note the contrast with the detached path: spawn_detached_child (src/sase/agent/detached_child.py:93) reserves a globally unique timestamp via reserve_launch_timestamp_batch(1), so out-of-process spawns are already protected. The in-process path has no equivalent.

REPRODUCTION: observed under the sase-p8.6 end-to-end pipe harness (tests/fakey/test_pipe_e2e.py), which drives two hand-offs back to back with no human latency between them. A human-paced hand-off almost never lands in one second, so this is currently a test-harness and fast-chain hazard rather than a routine user-visible failure — but a scripted chain, a retry storm, or a faster host can reach it, and the failure is silent metadata loss rather than an error.

SCOPE: give the in-process path the same uniqueness guarantee the detached path already has — either route create_followup_artifacts through reserve_launch_timestamp_batch, or make create_artifacts_directory detect an existing directory and allocate a distinct name. Verify with a test that creates two follow-up artifact dirs without advancing the clock and asserts both metas survive.
